mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at low levels (below 5.5%) compresses discount rates and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE falls below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer spending and economic activity, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between the joint increase of HOUST and RSAFS and positive 60-day SPX returns is not significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of industrial production growth (INDPRO above 100), the S&P 500 tends to rise as manufacturing activity supports corporate profits, but this effect is only active during expansionary regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is above 100 during expansionary industrial cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation (PAYEMS) indicates improving job market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 315.0 (current level 313.207) signals inflationary pressures that prompt central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 315.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL above 315) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS above 5.0%) indicates an active monetary tightening cycle, which suppresses equity valuations and generates negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL above 315 and FEDFUNDS above 5.0% does not produce negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 22700 billion), the S&P 500 tends to rise as economic expansion supports corporate earnings, but this effect is only active in the early stages of the business cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 is above 22700 during early-cycle expansion.
